newsitem.title: USA: Michael Foods to exit French fry business.
newsitem.headline: Michael Foods to exit French fry business.

text.p: Michael Foods Inc on Thursday said it decided to exit the frozen French fry business this year and took pretax charges of $22.7 million against its 1996 earnings to cover costs of the move.
Michael Foods said the decision was driven by higher raw material costs and increasing price pressures in the french fry market.
The company reported a 1996 fourth-quarter loss of $10.9 million, or $0.56 a share, after the pretax charge of $22.7 million.
Michael Foods processes and distributes egg products, refrigerated grocery products, frozen and refrigerated potato products and specialty dairy products.
Feed costs rose about 50 percent last year, which depressed Egg Products Division earnings, Ostrander said. The outlook for feed costs is more favorable for 1997.
The company's value-added egg products lines, especially Easy Eggs, performed well and were showing good momentum in the new year, he said.
The Refrigerated Distribution Division recorded strong earnings growth last year, while the Dairy Products Division showed a more moderate increase, he said.
The Potato Products Division operated at a loss for the fourth quarter and the year. The loss partly reflected volume and pricing pressures for frozen French fries, he said.

Looking ahead, Ostrander said, "This year we should realize benefits in our Egg Products Division from reduced feed costs after the first quarter. We would also expect profitable operations in our refrigerated potato products business and continued earnings momentum in our refrigerated distribution and dairy products business segments. We also expect to begin to realize synergies from the recent acquisition of Papetti's later in the year."
Trading in Michael Foods shares was halted on Thursday afternoon pending an announcement.
